root_idea.summary: The root centers on difficulty, severity, and constrained or intricate circumstances, in contrast with ease.
root_idea.development: From this core notion, the lexical field extends to poverty or limited means, opposition and harsh dealing, reciprocal difficulty, entanglement, difficult childbirth, refractory animals, and certain left-sided usages. These extensions are lexical developments, not automatic meanings of every Quranic form.

senses.definition: To be mutually difficult or harsh; to disagree or make a matter difficult for one another.
senses.usage_conditions: A reciprocal construction, used of parties such as a buyer and seller or a husband and wife. In the Quranic usage, it describes mutual difficulty in arranging an affair.
An adjective applied to an affair, thing, or circumstance that is hard to accomplish or endure.
An adjective for a difficult affair, thing, day, or circumstance; the Quranic day-usage denotes a day on which matters become difficult or distressing.

senses.definition: Difficulty, hardship, straitness, or an intricate burden; the opposite of ease.
senses.usage_conditions: A general noun for difficult circumstances or what is hard to bear or accomplish. It can occur in contrast with يُسْرٌ and in constructions describing hardship accompanying or following another condition.

senses.definition: Financial difficulty; lack of means or wealth.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a person or situation in which money or resources are difficult to obtain, especially in the context of a debt or financial obligation.

senses.definition: A state or period of hardship.
senses.usage_conditions: A conventional expression for difficult circumstances or a difficult period, including the Quranic reference to a time of hardship.

senses.definition: The difficult course or condition, contrasted with ease.
senses.usage_conditions: A feminine nominal form used with the preposition لِـ in the Quranic expression meaning toward or into difficulty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be obstructed in passing out, referring to what is in the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily-function construction describing contents that will not come forth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be hard, ungentle, or ill-natured in dealing with affairs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or disposition characterized by little gentleness, harshness, or narrowness of temperament.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To act adversely toward, oppose, or straiten someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction describing opposition or making matters difficult for another person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become severe, rigorous, afflictive, or adverse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of time or fortune when it turns harsh toward someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel that is untrained or difficult to manage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially a she-camel ridden or laden before training, or taken during the first stage of training.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to raise its tail while running or after conception.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage can describe a camel signaling after conception or displaying spirited or refractory movement while running.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To press an insolvent debtor for payment, refusing to defer collection until ease; a creditor who does this.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A debt-collection construction in which payment is difficult for the debtor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To force or compel someone against his or her will.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage includes compelling someone to do an act and taking property against the owner's wish.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Left-handed; one whose principal strength or use is in the left hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form can also denote the left hand or arm. The usage concerns bodily sidedness, not difficulty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come upon or approach someone from the right side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized verbal construction with a personal object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To treat or behave toward someone with hardness, harshness, or ill nature.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form III verbal noun مُعَاسَرَةٌ is presented as the contrary of مُيَاسَرَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter a state of difficulty, become poor, or lose property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a person who passes from means or prosperity into financial difficulty or reduced power.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To experience difficulty in childbirth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a woman in labor or of a camel whose young is difficult to deliver.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to fail to conceive during the year after mating.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized camel-breeding usage and is distinguished from difficulty in managing or riding the animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of spun thread, to become entangled so that it cannot be unraveled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized application reported with disagreement about whether this sense should instead be expressed by تَغَسَّرَ with غين.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ride a she-camel before it has been trained.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction refers to taking and riding a camel while it remains difficult to manage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To utter speech without prior preparation or deliberate formulation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form VIII usage describing speech produced without measuring or preparing it in the mind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek, desire, or demand something in which one experiences or expects difficulty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form X construction focused on seeking or demanding a difficult matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Poverty, scant possessions, or limited wealth or power.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical specialization of the hardship field, distinct from the general Quranic noun sense of difficulty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something difficult for a person, or a portion or circumstance in which someone experiences difficulty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In an idiomatic contrast with مَيْسُورٌ, it may describe what is difficult for someone or behavior that treats someone harshly rather than gently.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A named tribe of jinn or a land inhabited by jinn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a separate noun distinguished by its vocalization and lexical identity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most difficult, hard, strait, or intricate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative adjective applied to a thing, affair, circumstance, or difficult day; it is also used of an unfortunate day.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ambidextrous; able to use both hands alike.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed descriptive expression, distinct from the ordinary sense of أَعْسَرُ as left-handed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Characterized by a predominance or distinguishing feature on the left side, especially in a bird's wing or feathers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to pigeons, eagles, or feathers when the left-side primary feathers are more numerous or white.

lane_unit_coverage.note: General difficulty and hardening are covered by the Quranic difficulty and adjective senses.
Forcing or compelling against the will.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the compelling sense.
Taking property against its owner's will.
Seeking or demanding a difficult matter.
Quran examples of the core difficulty sense.
Proverbial illustration of difficulty versus ease.
The معسور lexical branch and harsh-treatment idiom.
Poverty and the difficult-course or difficult-circumstance sense of عُسْرَى.
Named period or circumstance of hardship.
The Quran citation interprets a form from يسر as leading to punishment or a difficult case, not a supplied QAC form of عسر.
Separate jinn tribe or land noun.
Difficult-to-attain want is an illustrative application of the adjective.
Comparative adjective applied to a day.
A creditor who presses an insolvent debtor.

cautions: The public verb headword تَعَاسَرَ is normalized from the Quranic inflected form تَعَاسَرْتُمْ to the standard perfect citation form.

The specialized thread usage of تَعَسَّرَ is reported with disagreement over whether the form should instead be تَغَسَّرَ; it is retained as a Classical usage rather than treated as certain Quranic evidence.
One Lane citation under عُسْرٌ interprets فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ as leading to punishment or a difficult case, but that cited expression belongs to يسر and no corresponding QAC form is supplied here.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: lane-unit:Esr:3201:g1:sub8 materially discusses the interpretation of فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ, but it cannot be assigned confidently to a supplied Quranic form of the root عسر because the cited expression is from the contrasting root يسر.
